The flag of Tonga consists of a red field containing a white canton in the upper hoist-side corner, with a smaller red cross (formed by the union of a horizontal rectangle and a vertical rectangle) contained inside the canton. Consequently, every pixel of any rasterization takes one of only two values: \(a\) (red regions) or \(b\) (white regions).

Any such matrix \(M\) may therefore be expressed as the linear combination
\[
M = b\cdot J + (a-b)\cdot C,
\]
where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix (rank 1) and \(C\) is the 0-1 indicator of the red set. The red set itself decomposes into three rectangular blocks:
- the entire flag (one rectangle),
- the complement of the canton inside the flag (one rectangle),
- the cross inside the canton (union of two rectangles).

Each rectangular indicator is an outer product of two indicator vectors and therefore has rank 1. Hence \(C\) has rank at most 3, which immediately implies
\[
\operatorname{rank}(M)\le 4.
\]
When the rasterization is fine enough that the horizontal and vertical dividing lines of the canton and cross fall between distinct rows and columns, and when \(a\neq b\), the four summands are linearly independent; consequently rank 4 is attained.

Thus the maximal possible rank is exactly 4.
